SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
He is named from the first return under Cyrus to the work of Darius's second year; Scripture gives no term of office.
FROM THE RETURN (538 BC OR SOON AFTER) TO THE TEMPLE'S COMPLETION (515 BC), ON PARKER AND DUBBERSTEIN'S TABLES
These are the bounds of the events Scripture names: Cyrus's first year at Babylon began in 538, and Darius's sixth year ended early in 515. Zerubbabel is not named at the completion itself.
KEIL (1872): THE RETURN IN 536 BC
Keil dates Cyrus's first year, and so the return, to 536; the end-point is Parker and Dubberstein's.
Yes: Sheshbazzar was Zerubbabel's Babylonian name
C. F. Keil (1873); H. E. Ryle (1893)

Sheshbazzar is the governor Cyrus appointed, who led the return and laid the foundation (Ezra 1:11; 5:14–16), the work Ezra 3 and Zechariah give to Zerubbabel. Keil compares the Babylonian names given to Daniel and his friends. Ezra 1:8 Ezra 5:14–16 Ezra 3:8 [29][33]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say when Zerubbabel's governorship began or ended, or how he died.
Ezra does not name him at the temple's completion and dedication (Ezra 6:14–18).
Scripture does not say whether he was the unnamed "Tirshatha" of Ezra 2:63 and Nehemiah 7:65, 70.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textEzra, Nehemiah and Haggai call him "the son of Shealtiel"; 1 Chronicles lists him among "the sons of Pedaiah"; Matthew has "Salathiel begat Zorobabel". Ezra 3:2 Nehemiah 12:1 Haggai 1:1 1 Chronicles 3:19 Matthew 1:12
From the textLuke's genealogy also names "Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel"; the site keeps that verse on a separate person record. Luke 3:27
From the textThe site's record for him also holds Sheshbazzar's verses, following one view; this page shows that question as views, below. Ezra 1:8 Ezra 5:14
